findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "estimate_service_request" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_message_to_vendor" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_vendors, get_vendor, send_message_to_vendor, prepare_quote_request · Private data: send_message_to_vendor · Public sink: send_message_to_vendor, prepare_quote_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_vendors, get_vendor, send_message_to_vendor, prepare_quote_request · Private data: send_message_to_vendor · Public sink: send_message_to_vendor, prepare_quote_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_services" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
